source: Make a forest game and add a flashlight to see the darkness and also make it night time. and make it realistic and explore the forest to find more stuff and things and houses and items.

image_prompt.text: Winding dirt tracks threading the forest, readable in the dark
Isolated forest houses standing among the trees, visible enough to pull the player toward them
Hidden cutouts behind overgrowth and fallen trees that reward poking around
The whole forest at night, dense and dark, lit only by moonlight so the beam of a handheld light is the main source of visibility

layout_placement.text: Loose items and things to find scattered through the forest and around the houses

notes: Time of day is load-bearing here (night, darkness) and there is no field for it, so it is written into the image entry and the theme.
A flashlight is a handheld light with no spatial footprint — no option covers it and the layout cannot express it.
If the forest houses are meant to be enterable this becomes P3; the prompt only says the player finds them.

open_questions.ask: Is finding the items the whole game, or is something in the forest hunting you?
How far should the forest run — a few minutes of walking, or a large open area you can get lost in?

theme: Realistic — dense nighttime woodland, weathered timber, no stylization

coverage_missing.ask: Is collecting the items the whole game, or is there a threat or an objective to finish?
How large should the forest be?
Are the houses enterable, or just landmarks you find?

answers.ask: Is finding the items the whole game, or is something in the forest hunting you?
answers.answer: Finding and exploring for items and houses is the whole game; nothing is hunting the player.

answers.ask: How far should the forest run — a few minutes of walking, or a large open area you can get lost in?
answers.answer: Use a forest that takes a few minutes to walk across, with enough paths and points of interest to explore.
